The retained sourced research records: CPV-controlled selection and repression preclude competitive government choice; constitutional Assembly voting, removal and term procedures still matter separately. Focused interpretation: Party-directed technical administration and controlled Assembly selection coexist with formal referendum procedures. The Assembly controls referendum initiation; citizen signatures alone do not trigger a binding ordinary-law vote, and effective independent checks remain limited. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.  This is a substantive conditional judgement: the described case for functioning government or collective continuity competes with the described limits on independent discretion or public consent. Neither unqualified permission nor unqualified prohibition best represents that tension. It is not a default for absent evidence. axes.brief:
Actual restrictions on political expression, assembly and movement coexist with surveillance and strong preventive security control.
Focused bank 3.0.0 reassessment: Surveillance, political house arrest and strong restrictions on independent organisation support broad authority in practice. Identity and security searches favour qualified permission, acknowledging incomplete consolidation of their precise general thresholds. Formal courts do not establish prompt independent recourse for political movement restrictions.
Focused bank 4.0.0 reassessment: Health and security administration favour qualified restrictions. Political suppression is broader than the new reviewed-court or protected-group mechanisms and does not establish impartial enforcement.
axes.counterEvidence:
Formal privacy/trial rights and ordinary legal procedures remain; exact retention, random stops, home warrants and civilian firearms are educated extrapolations rather than invented statutes.
Focused review: distinguish targeted warrants from bulk records, document possession from compulsory carrying, courts in law from effective prompt recourse, and notification/registration from discretionary association permission. Surveillance, political house arrest and strong restrictions on independent organisation support broad authority in practice. Identity and security searches favour qualified permission, acknowledging incomplete consolidation of their precise general thresholds. Formal courts do not establish prompt independent recourse for political movement restrictions. Earlier evidence limitations remain; new questions do not establish empirical calibration.
Focused review: distinguish adult shared-space outbreak conditions from purely personal paternalism, reviewed preventive controls from unreviewed detention, limited threat-area searches from routine suspicionless search, and nonviolent group-hatred incitement from criticism or moral-content censorship. Health and security administration favour qualified restrictions. Political suppression is broader than the new reviewed-court or protected-group mechanisms and does not establish impartial enforcement. Earlier evidence limitations remain; new questions do not establish empirical calibration.
